summary.text: A refrigerator is a thermally insulated compartment with a heat pump that moves heat from its inside to the outside, cooling the inside below room temperature.
The cold slows the reproduction of bacteria so food spoils more slowly, and the best range for perishable food is 3 to 5 °C.
Most household fridges and freezers use a vapor compression cycle, a technology first built in 1834, and home models were invented in 1913.

facts.label: Cooling method
facts.value: Vapor compression cycle in most household units

facts.label: What it replaced
facts.value: The icebox, used for almost a century and a half

items.prompt: Leftover soup lasts for days in a cold kitchen box but goes off within a day on the counter. What makes the difference?

options.label: The cold removes all the bacteria from the soup
The cold seals the soup away from air
The cold slows how fast bacteria reproduce
The cold turns bacteria into harmless food

items.explain: The low temperature reduces the reproduction rate of bacteria, so spoilage is slower.

items.prompt: Ice cream stays solid in one compartment, while milk stays liquid but cold in another. What sets the freezer apart?

options.label: It holds its contents below the freezing point of water
It keeps contents just over freezing
It runs without any heat pump
It matches the fridge section exactly

items.explain: A fridge maintains a temperature a few degrees above freezing, while a freezer keeps contents below the freezing point of water.

items.prompt: A fridge makes its inside colder than the room. Where does the heat that was inside go?

options.label: It is destroyed by the insulation
It is stored in the door
It is locked into the frozen food
It is moved out into the surrounding room

items.explain: The heat pump transfers heat from the inside to the external environment, cooling the inside below the room's temperature.

items.prompt: Before electric refrigerators, how did a typical family keep food cool through most of the year?

options.label: Boxes of ice or snow, in iceboxes and icehouses
Small Peltier coolers for drinks
Vapor compression units in each kitchen
Freon-filled cellars

items.explain: Icehouses and iceboxes, packed with ice or snow, provided cool storage before electric refrigerators arrived.

items.prompt: A family buys a large amount of meat on sale and eats it slowly over several weeks. What appliance feature makes this practical?

options.label: A beverage chiller
A freezer compartment
A built-in kitchen frame
An ice dispenser door

items.explain: Freezers let people buy perishable food in bulk and eat it at leisure.

items.prompt: Long before electricity, ancient Iranian yakhchāls kept things cool. What principles did they rely on?

options.label: Pumping heat with a compressor
Burning fuel to drive away warmth
Evaporative and radiative cooling
Chemical freezing mixtures

items.explain: Ancient Iranians used a form of cooler based on evaporative cooling and radiative cooling, with insulated domes and wind-catchers.
